Experiments on three long-video understanding benchmarks show that OTFS consistently outperforms strong training-free baselines. Codes are available at https://github.com/barry664/OTFS.

title: NeoWorld-3: From Pixels to Code-Defined Physical Worlds
authors: Eachen Soong, Zijian Niu, Haoran Xu, Yihong Dong, Yunbo Wang, Xiaokang Yang
abstract: Simulation-ready world reconstruction demands physical interactivity beyond visual realism, which existing black-box 3D generation fails to deliver. We present NeoWorld-3, a coding-agent framework that reconstructs interactive 3D worlds from visual observations via tunable, executable programs. At its core, NeoSDK provides the underlying computational engine for low-level geometries, part composition, differentiable parameter refinement, and physics validation. At the same time, NeoMCP exposes these capabilities as structured, tool-callable APIs for vision-language agents to visually inspect, edit code, and iteratively refine programs. Through a hierarchical coordinator-worker architecture, the framework scales seamlessly from standalone articulated objects to complex compositional scenes. Evaluations across object-level and scene-level reconstruction benchmarks demonstrate that NeoWorld-3 achieves state-of-the-art geometric fidelity and physical readiness. Crucially, manipulation trajectories planned within our reconstructed twins achieve successful zero-shot execution on a physical dual-arm robot, completing the Real-Sim-Real loop.

title: Adaptive Traversal Tubes for Posture-Aware Navigation of Bipedal Humanoids
authors: Zijian Ge
abstract: Bipedal humanoids can change their effective footprint by adjusting body yaw, enabling both narrow-passage traversal and socially aware yielding. This paper presents a posture-aware navigation framework centered on \emph{Adaptive Traversal Tubes} (ATT), \emph{Interval Velocity--Heading} (IVH) control, and a sidestep-enhanced AMP locomotion prior. ATT represents a behavior-feasible corridor width field along a reference path, unifying geometric clearance and social comfort into a continuous signal. IVH maps this width to a continuous frontal-to-sidestep posture schedule and omnidirectional velocity commands. A velocity-conditioned AMP policy, trained with GVHMR-retargeted frontal/sidestep motions and coupled \((v_x,v_y)\) tracking rewards, is designed to improve transition stability over a generic locomotion controller while remaining interchangeable with the default onboard policy. This preprint presents the full method; a planned evaluation protocol on a Unitree G1 is outlined, with quantitative results to follow. Demo videos of MuJoCo simulation and real-robot deployment are available at: github.com/lborogzj997/Humanoid-Navigation-in-Crowds-and-Narrow-Spaces.

title: Minorization and exponential ergodicity for degenerate diffusions with countable switching
authors: Yuzhong Cheng
abstract: We establish a local-minorization criterion for diffusions with countably many state-dependent switching regimes, even when every frozen transition law is singular. One regular controlled path yields a common absolutely continuous component for nearby initial states, with rate positivity required only at the switching locations. The proof controls a family of Brownian perturbations and its derivatives while retaining a path restriction for the switching likelihood. Controlled entrance and a joint Lyapunov inequality then give weighted exponential ergodicity. A concrete coefficient and rank criterion and degenerate network examples illustrate the result.

title: PhonoBridge: Error-Aware Phoneme-Mediated EMG-to-Text Reconstruction
authors: Wen Qiu, Jiacheng Zhang, Xuanda Chen, Siqi Cai, Haizhou Li
abstract: Electromyography (EMG) provides a non-invasive means of decoding silently articulated speech into text, but accurate decoding remains challenging due to limited availability of paired EMG-text data. We introduce PhonoBridge, a two-stage framework comprising a channel-aware EMG-to-phoneme frontend and a large language model (LLM) backend for text reconstruction. The frontend is trained on paired EMG-text data that consists of channel-wise feature extraction, cross-channel fusion, and electrode embeddings. With phonemes as the intermediate representation, we expand the backend's training data by converting LibriSpeech transcripts into phoneme-text pairs without additional EMG recordings. To adapt the LLM to frontend noise, we introduce Error-Profile-Guided Augmentation (EPGA), which perturbs transcript-derived phoneme sequences according to error patterns estimated from frontend predictions, generating additional training pairs for the LLM. On the Open Vocabulary silent-speech dataset, PhonoBridge achieves 24.77% WER, outperforming the previously reported best of 28.27% on the same test split.

title: Neural Operator Splitting for Fluid Dynamics in Complex Geometry
authors: Jianxiang Li, Xi Deng, Hong Chul Nam, Anima Anandkumar
abstract: Solving dynamical systems in complex and diverse geometries remains challenging for both numerical solvers and learning-based surrogate models. We propose Neural Operator Splitting, a framework for learning fluid dynamics while preserving the physical structure of fractional-step numerical schemes. Instead of learning the full-step evolution monolithically, we decompose each time step into physically interpretable steps, and learn each operator separately using intermediate states from the underlying numerical solver. Guided by the linearity properties of the fractional steps, we introduce a conditional-linear Fourier neural operator (CL-FNO) whose linear state mappings are modulated by nonlinear conditioning on inputs such as boundary geometry. We further introduce two complementary strategies, symmetry sampling and corrective cycling, to mitigate error accumulation during autoregressive rollout. Experiments on 2D and 3D fluid flows with varying geometries and initial conditions show that our full model reduces mean relative $L^2$ rollout error by 68\% in 2D and 40\% in 3D compared with a single full-step neural operator. At comparable error levels, neural-operator inference is approximately $10^3$ times faster per step than the Monte Carlo solver.

title: A new class of smooth algebraic varieties with the density property and a counterexample to the Tóth-Varolin Conjecture
authors: Sushil Gorai
abstract: We prove that the smooth affine hypersurfaces \[ X_{m,n}=\{ζ^mz_0^n+ (1+z_1ζ)z_2+ζz_3^2=1\}\subset\mathbb{C}^5,\;\; m,n\geq 2, \] have the density property. For every odd integer $d\geq 3$, we identify $X_{d-1,d}$ with a Kaliman modification along a Brieskorn variety of type $(d,2,2,2)$. We prove that the fourfolds $X_{d-1,d}$ are diffeomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$ but not biholomorphic to $\mathbb{C}^4$. These, therefore, give counterexamples to the Tóth-Varolin conjecture.

title: Global exact controllability for Schrödinger equations with Lipschitz and logarithmic nonlinearities
authors: Lei Zhang, Xiuting Li
abstract: In this paper, we study global exact controllability of semilinear Schrödinger equations by localized internal additive controls. For every globally Lipschitz nonlinearity in arbitrary dimensions, we prove that any two $L^2$ states can be connected in any prescribed positive time, without smallness assumptions on the states or the Lipschitz constant. The result holds on smooth bounded Euclidean domains under a local convex-phase condition, and on an interval with any nonempty open control region. It also extends to compact Riemannian manifolds under the corresponding phase condition. In one dimension, we further establish controllability for logarithmic nonlinearities of the form \[ f(z)=zφ(|z|)+\mathfrak g(z), \] where $φ$ is real-valued, $\mathfrak g$ is globally Lipschitz, and $r|φ'(r)|\leq D(1+|\log r|)^γ$ with $0\leqγ<1/2$. For the endpoint case $γ=1/2$, we achieve the result by assuming the leading coefficient is sufficiently small. These results resolve the global Lipschitz controllability question raised by Zuazua \cite[Section~3]{Zuazua2003} in the stated geometric settings and establish its logarithmic extension within the specified one-dimensional classes.

title: PACE-MoE: Adaptive Domain Sampling and Domain-Specific LoRA for Medical Visual Grounding
authors: Zhenxuan Wang, Jisheng Dang, Ronghao Lin, Bimei Wang, Jingwen Zhao, Wenjun Ma, Bin Hu, Qi Tian, Tat-Seng Chua
abstract: Medical visual grounding requires models to align clinical descriptions with spatial evidence across heterogeneous imaging domains. However, existing multi-domain post-training strategies typically rely on fixed domain sampling and shared parameter updates, overlooking the need to adapt both which domains receive training and where their updates are applied. To address this issue, we propose PACE-MoE, a policy-guided framework that jointly performs adaptive domain sampling and domain-specific adaptation for medical visual grounding. PACE dynamically assesses the training value of each imaging domain from current-policy feedback and progressively adjusts domain coverage through domain admission, replay, and final all-domain balancing. Meanwhile, domain-specific LoRA adapters route updates to the corresponding imaging domains while preserving the pretrained backbone and visual encoder. This coordinated design aligns training-data allocation with parameter adaptation without modifying the original reward formulation or Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) objective. Experiments across seven medical imaging domains show that PACE-MoE consistently improves grounding performance over fixed-domain training, achieving a 3.64% relative improvement in mean box IoU over the Vanilla baseline. Under matched domain-specific adapter architectures, adaptive sampling alone further improves mean box IoU by 2.07%, demonstrating the benefit of policy-guided domain allocation. These results establish coordinated data-parameter routing as an effective strategy for multi-domain medical visual grounding.

title: U torsion structure in Heegaard Floer homology
authors: Yuhui Chen, Shunyu Wan
abstract: We construct infinite families of Brieskorn spheres with three singular fibers for which the difference between the largest and the second largest length of U-torsion in their Heegaard Floer homology $HF^-$ increases to infinity as the family parameter increases. In particular, these families give a negative answer to the strong geography restriction on rational homology spheres. As an application, these families give the examples of integer homology spheres that are neither surgery on a knot nor large surgery on links.

title: A cut-and-project set which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice
authors: Alan Haynes
abstract: We construct a cut-and-project set in a totally irrational plane in $\mathbb{R}^3$, with a compact window which is the closure of its interior and has countable boundary, which is not bi-Lipschitz equivalent to a lattice. This answers a question of Burago and Kleiner about cut-and-project sets, and shows in particular that the hypothesis of boundary measure zero is not enough to guarantee bi-Lipschitz equivalence to a lattice. Since our set has uniform density, it also shows that a non-rectifiable Delone set need not encode a non-realisable density, answering a question of Bhat and Dymond.

title: Ensemble-Aware Structural Encoding (EASE): Conditioning Protein Encoders on Peptide Conformational Ensembles
authors: Ruoyao Zhang, Hongxuan Li, Jie Peng, Tianlong Chen
abstract: Protein foundation models provide transferable representations for downstream peptide prediction tasks. However, existing representations typically reduce a peptide to a single sequence or structure, which may miss conformational variability relevant to key peptide properties, including antibacterial activity, hemolysis, toxicity, stability, and binding. For example, protease resistance correlates more strongly with conformational dynamics measured by hydrogen exchange than with average helicity. Therefore, we introduce Ensemble-Aware Structural Encoding (EASE), a framework for effectively extracting structural information from conformational ensembles for peptide representation. To extract useful information from noisy conformers, EASE selects central conformers representing a peptide's major structural states and fuses their individual representations with a permutation-invariant operator to produce a peptide-level representation for downstream prediction. We then evaluate our framework on six peptide property-prediction tasks under leakage-controlled splits. Against matched single-structure baselines, EASE improves performance consistently on six tasks with a mean absolute gain of about 3.0% across two structural encoders. Gains keep growing as we add conformers through K=20. A single peptide conformer therefore provides a limited basis for structural representation, whereas our framework distilling and fusing multiple conformers yields a more informative representation.

title: PAR: Progress-Aligned Recurrence for Length Generalization in State Tracking
authors: Pan Wang, Yihao Hu, Guangyuan Dong, Yitong Lin, Hang Wang, Zimi Liu, Zhihao Wen, Jianshe Li, Jiang-Ming Yang, Wei Wu, Yongqi Tong
abstract: Looped language models can run more iterations at test time, but additional iterations need not help them solve longer problems. For sequential state tracking, final-answer supervision does not specify how far each iteration should advance, and repeated updates can change the scale of the recurrent state. We introduce \textbf{Progress-Aligned Recurrence (PAR)}, which trains the prediction at iteration $k$ to match the state after the first $k$ operations and rescales recurrent states to their first-iteration norms. On swap-$S_5$, a Qwen2.5-0.5B model trained on at most 32 moves achieves 95.5\% mean full-state accuracy at 512 moves, or $16\times$ the training length, compared with 55.7\% reported for RLT and 0.8\% for explicit chain of thought on the same backbone. Controlled $S_5$ ablations show that removing norm anchoring reduces the extrapolation factor from $16\times$ to below $2.2\times$, and replacing progress-aligned targets with final-answer supervision reduces it to at most $8\times$. A learned completion readout selects when to answer without a supplied stopping depth. When intermediate labels are unavailable, prefix self-distillation induces the correspondence from shorter problem prefixes using only final answers. The gains apply across sequential state-tracking tasks, establishing the task structure required for depth extrapolation. These findings support training intermediate predictions and state scale together to make additional recurrent depth useful for longer problems.

title: Orbital Magnetization within Self-Consistent Hartree-Fock via an Envelope Theorem
authors: Daniel E Parker
abstract: Orbital magnetization is an elementary thermodynamic response function of a quantum system: the derivative of the grand potential with respect to magnetic field. However, naive perturbation theory is fraught with difficulties, as even infinitesimal magnetic fields shatter any bands into a Hofstadter butterfly spectrum. Even at the self-consistent Hartree-Fock (mean field) level, rigorous formulas for the orbital magnetization have only become available within the last year. This work provides a straightforward derivation of orbital magnetization at the mean field level using a completely real-space approach. The key tools used are the magnetic perturbation theory developed in the 1960s and an envelope theorem, which is a standard result in the calculus of variations. For simplicity, we restrict to insulating states at zero temperature on the infinite plane. We also discuss the natural connections to projected position operators and quantum geometry, as well as practical numerical computations.

title: Local Allow, Global Deny: Why Per-Action Authorization Does Not Compose in LLM Agents
authors: Anmol Pandey, Aditya Jain, Liang Chen, Carsten Maple
abstract: Autonomous LLM agents act through tools under per-action authorization: a local guard screens each tool call in isolation. We show that local authorization does not compose into global authorization. A compositional authorization failure (CAF) is a locally authorized execution, or a pair of locally authorized executions, that violates a global policy spanning intent, purpose, provenance, consent, and delegation. We characterize CAFs along two axes, expressiveness (single-trace safety versus relational k-safety) and observability (a ladder of monitor profiles). Our central result is an impossibility: relational purpose violations form a 2-safety hyperproperty with no per-trace locus of blame, so a per-action monitor that never raises a false alarm detects none of them, independent of the underlying model or decision procedure; they become visible only under cross-execution monitoring, which none of the six guardrails we survey implements. We make this constructive with AL-SYNTH, a SAT/SMT synthesizer (using no language model) that emits minimal CAF witnesses, each checked against an exhaustive oracle. The empirical signature is sharp: across nine LLM judges the per-action view approves the synthesized witness almost without exception, blocking it at a rate comparable to a benign control, yet the same models flag it when shown the two executions together. Per-action authorization is therefore structurally insufficient for relational policy conjuncts not reducible to single-trace safety: to bound them, a monitor must compare executions or accept false alarms.

title: Analysis and Optimization of Age of Information in Large-Scale Random Access Networks
authors: Yueqi Chen, Siqi Fan, Zhuoyi Zhao, I-Hong Hou, Igor Kadota
abstract: We consider a large-scale network where multiple nodes transmit time-sensitive information via a shared channel to a wireless base station using a Carrier-Sense Multiple Access (CSMA) protocol. In this network, packet transmissions from different nodes are interdependent, making it challenging to analyze and optimize information freshness, captured by the Age of Information (AoI) metric. In this paper, we develop a tractable analytical framework for analyzing and optimizing the AoI. By combining mean-field approximation with first return time and renewal reward analysis, the proposed approach provides a fast, tractable, and accurate AoI approximation that explicitly accounts for carrier sensing, enabling us to quickly find the network parameters that minimize AoI. Since the framework is built on a finite-state Markov representation of the CSMA protocol, it applies to a broad class of Random Access systems. As a concrete example, we study age-threshold CSMA protocols and derive closed-form or efficiently computable AoI approximations under different protocol settings. We validate the proposed AoI analysis via extensive simulations, demonstrating a tight agreement between analysis and simulation.

title: WORTH Benchmark: Evidence Discovery under Not-Fully-Cooperative Information -- A Two-Episode Pilot
authors: Bo Zou, Chao Xu
abstract: Existing reasoning evaluations typically provide task-relevant information to models as available premises, rarely examining concurrently how models discover evidence autonomously and how information presentation within narratives guides or obscures judgment. This paper proposes the WORTH Benchmark: models read original mystery narratives without clue annotations, autonomously select key clue sentences, identify case participants, and explain their reasoning process. The narrative materials are designed by professional authors such that evidence facilitating reasoning coexists with narrative arrangements that delay the revelation of truth. We report a pilot experiment under full-story conditions across two episodes, conducting a total of 70 formal runs on models, of which 67 runs are content-scorable. Scoring separately records hits on author-designated key clue sentences and participant selections; natural language explanations are used for case diagnosis and are not scored independently. The results show that clue hits and participant judgments are not synchronized; across 37 content-scorable runs in Episode 02, 31 runs simultaneously selected the same set of incorrect participants, while adjacent suspicion-oriented and exoneration-oriented sentences were selected 25 times and 0 times, respectively. These phenomena illustrate the diagnostic value of component-wise analysis and suggest that not-fully-cooperative informational relationships may influence evidence selection and judgment. This study only implements full-story conditions for two episodes, and does not establish stable model rankings or infer general mechanisms on this basis; human player records have not yet been cleaned, and this version does not report human-model comparisons.

title: Sensitivity-Orthogonal Residual Learning for Adaptive Sideslip and Cornering Stiffness Estimation
authors: Kyoungtae Ji, Dongyeol Won, Kyoungseok Han
abstract: Online adaptation of the cornering stiffness keeps a model-based sideslip estimator valid as tires change, but competes with learned model correction for the same filter innovation. A corrector with enough parameters can absorb the innovation pattern that a stiffness change produces, and adaptation is suppressed while the fit improves. We propagate the stiffness sensitivities of the predicted measurements through the vehicle states and construct a corrector orthogonal to them. A null-space parameterization enforces the constraint without a penalty coefficient and preserves the static least-squares stiffness estimate on each identification segment. In full-vehicle simulation, the stiffness response of the unconstrained corrector declines as its parameter count grows, whereas the orthogonal corrector responds at least as fully as the uncorrected filter at all sizes and lowers sideslip error by 12.7% to 22.0%. In a simulated drive with a stiffness step, the orthogonal corrector adapts as quickly as the uncorrected filter and lowers sideslip error during and after the transient. On public real-vehicle data, the 430-parameter unconstrained corrector loses most of its response to deliberate offsets of the filter's nominal stiffness, whereas the orthogonal corrector of the same size retains most of it, with a sideslip error slightly above the uncorrected filter's.

title: Bridging Digital Deception and Physical Fidelity: A Spatio-Temporal Attack on Cognitive Radars
authors: Tongrun Xing, Yongjun Dai, Xuan Liao, Zhiwen Zhang, Tong Zhou, Longlong Zhang, Tian Jiang
abstract: As cognitive radars evolve towards the end-to-end processing of one-dimensional complex baseband sequences, deep networks face severe adversarial threats. However, existing attacks encounter dual limitations in practical electronic warfare: low cross-architecture transferability and severe vulnerability to physical channel distortions, which degrades their tactical reliability. To overcome these bottlenecks, we propose a physical prior-driven Segmented Spatio-Temporal Attack (SSTA). First, a global-local feature decoupling segmentation mechanism interrupts the adversarial gradients' dependence on long-range sequence coherence, bridging the cross-architecture feature gap. Second, moving beyond static norm constraints devoid of physical semantics, we abstract channel distortions into differentiable spatio-temporal operators, integrating them into momentum iterations via an Expectation over Transformation (EoT) strategy. Comprehensive cross-evaluations across 9 heterogeneous models spanning CNNs, RNNs, and Transformers demonstrate that SSTA outperforms the state-of-the-art baseline by 10.36% in Average Black-Box Attack Success Rate. Furthermore, baseband equivalent simulations confirm that the generated waveforms survive extreme physical distortions and, after matched filtering, achieve zero main-lobe attenuation (0 dB) with noise floor lift strictly within Constant False Alarm Rate tolerances. SSTA successfully unifies digital-domain deception and physical-domain fidelity, providing crucial support for CEW security assessment.

title: Why Static Probes Fail: Context Determines Deception Feature Composition
authors: Yao Huang, Siyuan Chen, Zhenghan Zhou, Yinpeng Dong
abstract: With increasing autonomy, Large Language Models (LLMs) may engage in deceptive behaviors, such as scheming to pursue misaligned goals or sandbagging to escape oversight. Monitoring outputs alone is insufficient, as models can produce seemingly benign responses while harboring misaligned internal objectives. While mechanistic approaches like linear probing are promising, they rely on the assumption that deception corresponds to a single direction in representation space. We demonstrate that such single-direction probes fail to generalize across diverse deception scenarios. To bridge this gap, we propose representing deception as a multi-dimensional subspace rather than a single direction. Our method utilizes iterative orthogonal decomposition to identify complementary directions that capture distinct facets of deceptive intent. To effectively leverage these directions for detection, we find that static combinations prove brittle due to strong domain dependence across different scenarios. We therefore introduce a domain-adaptive gating mechanism that dynamically composes the extracted directions through few-shot adaptation at test time. With only 10 examples, our approach achieves an average AUROC of 0.97 and 94% recall at 5% FPR across all evaluated datasets, substantially outperforming existing methods.

title: Text-Anchored Modality Experts with Uncertainty-Guided Routing for Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
authors: Xiaohua Huang, Bingrui Lei, Xiuyan hao, Ling Zhou, Yuan Zong, Wenming Zheng, Guoying Zhao
abstract: Multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) aims to understand user-generated videos by integrating multiple modalities. Existing methods often treat modalities as symmetric, overlooking the fact that language provides a dominant semantic prior while nonverbal signals are complementary and noise-prone. To address this, we propose a Text-Anchored Modality Experts with Uncertainty-Guided Routing, termed TAME, that reformulates MSA as an uncertainty-guided refinement paradigm, where the language prior is calibrated and enhanced by selectively trusted nonverbal evidence. Specifically, TAME adopts an asymmetric Mixture-of-Modality-Experts framework, in which textual features act as a fixed and always-activated shared expert, while audio-textual and video-textual cross-modal branches serve as dynamically routed auxiliary experts. Furthermore, we introduce lightweight Prophet Heads to quantify the sample-level predictive uncertainty of each individual modality, and this uncertainty metric is further incorporated into the modality router to realize reliability-aware expert aggregation and fusion. Experiments on CMU-MOSI, CMU-MOSEI, and CH-SIMS datasets demonstrate that TAME achieves state-of-the-art performance on the majority of metrics while reducing parameter count by up to 78.7% and FLOPs by up to 41.2% over the mixture-of-expert baseline. %These results confirm that asymmetric expert construction with uncertainty-guided routing is an effective paradigm for MSA.

title: AudiPsy: Evidence-Grounded Multimodal Reasoning over Spoken Counseling Conversations for Depression Assessment
authors: Chuanbo Zhu, Run Luo, Weibo Zhao, Yue Li, Kun Qian, Qiang Qu, Yike Guo, Minghuan Tan, Wei Xue
abstract: Depression assessment from counseling speech requires integrating textual and acoustic psychological evidence across turns, yet existing end-to-end classification approaches lack explicit multimodal evidence interpretation and context-aware reasoning. We propose AudiPsy, an evidence-grounded omni-LLM for depression assessment over spoken counseling conversations. AudiPsy employs an Observation-Assessment-Summary (OAS) paradigm to integrate dialogue transcripts, textual and acoustic emotions, and textual-acoustic emotion incongruence into structured reasoning. OAS incrementally organizes multimodal observations, performs contextualized assessment, and maintains an evolving dialogue summary for subsequent turns. To support this framework, we construct AudiPsy-Counsel, a synthetic spoken counseling conversation corpus with multimodal context augmentation, and develop a unified three-stage curriculum for depression-oriented reasoning. Experiments on DAIC-WOZ demonstrate superior depression assessment performance over specialized depression detection methods and general-purpose speech/omni-LLMs, along with improved reasoning quality, while supplementary evaluation on EATD-Corpus supports AudiPsy's applicability to naturalistic conversations.

title: CityPaint: A Free Lunch from 2D Diffusion for City-Scale 3D Texturing
authors: Yuchen Zou, Lihuang Fang, Siyu Zhu, Xiao Hu
abstract: Generating high-fidelity, city-scale 3D environments plays a crucial role in applications such as virtual reality, gaming, and urban digital twins. However, the scarcity of real-world city-scale 3D training data forces existing methods to either stitch independently generated assets or learn from synthetic urban corpora, often sacrificing realism and global consistency. In contrast, 2D image data and their corresponding generative models are abundant and encode rich visual priors. To bridge this gap, we propose CityPaint, a novel framework that leverages 2D diffusion models to generate globally consistent city-scale 3D textures without relying on city-scale 3D training data. Specifically, CityPaint integrates geometric priors with the generative power of 2D diffusion models, introducing a robust top-$K$ camera baking strategy for iterative texture projection. To address the artifacts of 2D-to-3D projection, we further propose a decoupled refinement mechanism that separately optimizes terrain and building textures. Extensive experiments show that CityPaint produces globally coherent textures with fine local details and achieves favorable results against strong baselines in both visual quality and cross-view consistency.

title: Optimal Two-Mode Switching with Setup Costs for a Controlled Ornstein--Uhlenbeck Process
authors: Hongkun Xia, Dacheng Yao
abstract: We study an infinite-horizon discounted optimal switching problem for an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck process whose mean-reversion level can be switched between two values. Switching incurs positive, potentially asymmetric fixed costs, and the mode with the higher mean-reversion level entails an additional running cost. The revenue rate is proportional to the positive part of the state. We characterize the value function and identify parameter conditions under which an optimal policy either remains permanently in one mode after a possible costly initial switch or follows a threshold rule. The threshold formulation allows infinite boundaries and therefore includes one-way switching. A key technical contribution is to establish existence and uniqueness of the relevant solutions to the coupled nonlinear free-boundary equations arising from value-matching and smooth-fit conditions. In the corresponding parameter regimes, these solutions determine the finite switching thresholds and the coefficients of the candidate value functions. A verification argument then establishes the optimality of the resulting policies over all admissible switching strategies.

title: $\mathrm{v}$-numbers of powers of edge ideals of cubic circulant graphs
authors: Guangjun Zhu, Jiaxin Li, Yulin Hu
abstract: In this paper, we provide the exact formula for the $\mathrm{v}$-number of powers of the edge ideal of a cubic circulant graph $C_{2n}(a,n)$ with $1\le a<n$.

title: Adversarial Benchmarks and BenchDoor Attacks: Exploiting Benchmark Incentives for Backdoor Attacks
authors: Yixin Wu, Rachel Hong, Jamie Morgenstern, Tadayoshi Kohno
abstract: Machine learning benchmarks act as guideposts for model development and spur the creation of training datasets intended to improve benchmark scores. We introduce BenchDoor, a family of data poisoning attacks that exploits this incentive. Beyond preserving benign performance, BenchDoor requires benchmark gains that encourage adoption of data that also implants a backdoor. The adversary either manipulates a benchmark's training or test data, creating an adversarial benchmark, or supplies an independent training dataset while leaving the benchmark unchanged. We formalize five attack scenarios, including training on rewritten test examples and applying similarity-based decontamination. Across multiple-choice Q&A, text classification, and open-ended Q&A with Qwen and Gemma models, BenchDoor achieves positive benchmark gains for all 30 evaluated configurations, with held-out attack success rates of 82.33% to 100.00% at poisoning rates of 2% to 10%. Both objectives remain achievable after synthetic data generation and similarity-based decontamination, with attack success rates of at least 90.33%. These findings show how benchmarks can serve as attack vectors both through their own data and through training resources that deliver improvements on them.

title: Collision-aware Bayesian mitigation of photon loss in linear optical quantum circuits
authors: Seungwoo Kim, Seunghyun Ahn, Donguk Nam, Hyunho Cha, Jungwoo Lee
abstract: Photon loss is the dominant noise source in linear optical quantum circuits. Each lost photon turns an ideal n-photon outcome into a pattern with fewer photons, so the detector counts no longer follow the ideal output distribution, and the lossless events that do follow it become exponentially rare as the photon number grows. Discarding the lossy events (postselection) therefore wastes most of the data at realistic loss rates, and the ideal distribution has to be inferred from the lossy counts themselves. Recycling-based mitigation (Mills & Mezher, Quantum 2026; Quandela's photon_recycling) reweights lossy samples to recover lossless probabilities, but its estimators are biased and restricted to the no-collision sector, where each output mode holds at most one photon. We instead treat the raw counts as Multinomial observations under per-photon binomial loss and infer the ideal output distribution and the loss rate jointly from a Bayesian posterior, which extends naturally to outputs with collisions. On data from the independent Perceval simulator at the scale of prior work (n=4 photons in m=20 and m=10 modes), the posterior has lower KL divergence than both recycling and postselection at every tested loss rate in the no-collision benchmark. In the collision regime it recovers the loss rate and the collision-pattern probabilities, which recycling cannot estimate, and stays below recycling at every loss rate and below postselection except at low loss, where the two are comparable. Its advantage over recycling grows with the sample count, and it supplies credible intervals that the baselines lack.

title: A boundary approach to rigidity of $q$-Araki--Woods factors
authors: Yusuke Isono
abstract: In this paper, we study structural and rigidity properties of $q$-Araki--Woods factors arising from strongly continuous orthogonal representations of $\R$. We first introduce an AO-type boundary property that is formulated in terms of length projections on the $q$-Fock spaces, and prove that all $q$-Araki--Woods factors satisfy this condition. We next characterize uniform convergence of the associated malleable deformations. We then use these two ingredients as a substitute for weak containment in the coarse bimodule and deduce several rigidity theorems in the framework of Popa's deformation/rigidity theory. As a main consequence, we prove that every $q$-Araki--Woods factor is stably strongly solid. We also prove a normalizer rigidity theorem for inclusions arising from direct sum representations. Finally, we compute Connes' $τ$-invariant, and construct a continuum of pairwise non-isomorphic type $\mathrm{III}_1$ $q$-Araki--Woods factors with the same $τ$-invariant.

title: HealBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Evaluating Psychological Comfort in Text-to-Image Generation
authors: Junjie Xu, Yuzhe Yang, Rui Yang, Luwei Xiao, Wenxin Wu, Xingjiao Wu, Liang He
abstract: Despite advances in photorealism, semantic fidelity, and aesthetics, text-to-image generation and image editing remain understudied in a human-centered dimension: whether their outputs feel psychologically comforting. Grounded in cognitive evaluation theory, we define psychological comfort as an affective response shaped by viewers' appraisal of restorative and emotionally supportive visual cues. We introduce HealBench, a fine-grained benchmark of 30,000 high-quality image-text pairs spanning 19 categories and 92 subcategories, selected from 100,000 candidates through a human- and expert-in-the-loop pipeline combining vision-language model matching, human preference models, expert filtering, and exemplar-guided augmentation. We also construct HealBench-Eval, a feature-clustered evaluation set of 1,095 instances. Using HealBench-Eval, we conduct objective and subjective evaluations of 14 representative image generation models and prompt-rewriting strategies. Results reveal a gap between conventional visual quality and perceived comfort: strong semantic alignment and aesthetics do not guarantee emotionally restorative images. Reinforcement learning experiments further show that HealScorer can serve as a reward signal for assessing and improving the emotional and restorative quality of generated images. These findings establish psychological comfort as a distinct dimension of human-centered image generation and position HealBench as a foundation for affect-aware generative models.

title: Progressive Subset Selection and Cascaded Consistency for Unsupervised Vision-Language Model Adaptation
authors: Hao Yan, Guanghui Wang
abstract: Pretrained Vision-Language Models (PVLMs) achieve strong zero-shot recognition but often suffer performance degradation under target-domain shift. Unsupervised adaptation provides a practical way to improve target-domain performance without labeled data, but it remains challenging because pseudo-labels generated by the model can be unreliable and no labeled validation set is available for model selection or early stopping. We propose a simple framework for unsupervised PVLM adaptation that combines progressive margin-based subset selection with cascaded consistency learning. The subset selection strategy constructs a class-balanced pseudo-labeled set using prediction margins and gradually expands it during training, enabling adaptation to start from reliable supervision anchors before incorporating broader target-domain data. Cascaded consistency learning further exploits unlabeled samples by using temporally smoothed teacher predictions on weakly augmented views to supervise student predictions on strongly augmented views, with confidence filtering to reduce the influence of uncertain pseudo-labels. To preserve the pretrained embedding structure, the framework updates only normalization parameters in the visual encoder and class prototypes initialized from text prompts. Experiments across multiple recognition benchmarks with both CLIP and SigLIP backbones show consistent improvements over zero-shot baselines and competitive performance against recent unsupervised PVLM adaptation methods. These results suggest that progressive pseudo-label selection and teacher-guided consistency provide an effective and lightweight strategy for adapting PVLM classifiers without labeled target data.

title: Quantum Cryptanalysis on Two Feistel-Type Constructions
authors: Yan-Ying Zhu, Bin-Bin Cai, Fei Gao, Song Lin
abstract: With the rapid advancement of quantum computing, the security of traditional cryptographic systems is facing significant challenges. As a fundamental component of symmetric cryptography, block ciphers have attracted increasing attention regarding their quantum security in recent years. In this paper, we propose new quantum attacks on two Feistel-type constructions, i.e., New Structure IV and the lightweight block cipher LBlock, under the quantum chosen-plaintext attack (qCPA) model. First, we construct an 8-round quantum distinguisher for New Structure IV and perform an $r(r>12)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. Compared with Li et al.'s qCPA-based result presented at INSCRYPT 2024, our attack reduces the time complexity by a factor of $2^{n/2}$, where $n$ denotes the subkey length. Second, we design a 9-round quantum distinguisher for LBlock and extend it to an $r(r>15)$-round quantum key-recovery attack. The proposed quantum distinguisher covers one more round than Liu et al.'s automated-search distinguisher at ASIACRYPT 2025, which results in a $2^{16}$ reduction in the time complexity of our $r$-round quantum key-recovery attack on LBlock. Furthermore, by analyzing the structure of the round function and the key scheduling of LBlock, we reduce the subkey guess space for the 15-round attack from 76 bits to 52 bits, lowering the time complexity from \(O(2^{38})\) to \(O(2^{26})\) by a factor of \(2^{12}\).

title: On a Notion of Density Related to Restricted Diophantine Approximation
authors: Chance Sanford
abstract: We introduce notion of density for a subset of the natural numbers called the Diophantine density. First, we demonstrate that the Diophantine density is an abstract density in the sense of Di Nasso and Jin. Then we establish upper and lower bounds for the Diophantine density of a set and its complement respectively. We also exhibit a construction which allows us to find a set whose density can be any value between zero and one. Finally, we prove a restricted-denominator analog of Dirichlet's approximation theorem for sets of non-zero Diophantine density.

title: The Spectrum of the Discrete Mathieu Operator with Nonreal Coupling
authors: Frédéric Klopp, Izak Oltman
abstract: We study the discrete Mathieu operator with nonreal coupling in the large-period limit, using complex WKB methods for analytic finite-difference equations. We obtain quantization formulas in different regions of the complex energy plane. Away from the corners of the image of the classical symbol, these formulas involve cosines of classical action integrals with small analytic corrections to the actions. Near each corner, we derive a uniform quantization formula involving the reciprocal Gamma function. The quantization formulas constrain spectral accumulation to curves determined by the competing exponential terms. Numerical computations illustrate the resulting spectral geometry.

title: Securing Agentic Commerce Through Behavior-Aware Fraud Detection and Cybersecurity for Trusted AI-Agent Payment Authorization
authors: Kayode L. Ogunsusi
abstract: The growing use of autonomous artificial intelligence agents in digital commerce creates new security concerns involving agent impersonation, unauthorized payments, compromised agents, and misuse of delegated authority. This research introduces the Autonomous Commerce Agent Guard System (ACAGS), a cybersecurity framework combining supervised machine learning, behavioral analytics, agent-specific authorization controls, and explainable AI. The framework was evaluated using synthetic financial transaction data augmented with simulated agent characteristics and five adversarial scenarios. XGBoost was selected following comparisons with alternative classifiers. Across ten experimental runs, behavioral features improved mean F1-score from 52.12% to 67.49%, with agent-specific features increasing performance to 69.46%. The framework achieved detection rates of 99.77% for abnormal agent behavior, 99.73% for impersonation, and 100% for malicious delegation and authorization-scope violations. Compromised-agent detection reached 72.27%. ACAGS also supported APPROVE, REVIEW, and REJECT authorization outcomes, with SHAP explanations providing model interpretability. The results demonstrate the potential of combining behavioral intelligence and delegated authorization controls to strengthen simulated agentic-commerce payment security, while highlighting the need for validation using real-world transactions.

title: Rational polynomial solvability reduces to stratifiability of semilinear sets
authors: Michaël Cadilhac
abstract: A semilinear set is stratifiable if it is a finite union of linear sets whose periods have at most two nonzero coordinates, with no two periods in one component connecting alternating pairs of coordinates. We give a computable many-one reduction from the existence of a rational zero of an integer polynomial to deciding stratifiability. After the classical reduction to quadratic systems, we reduce rational solvability of these systems to a problem we call finite separation by Cartesian products of rational linear forms. Its input consists of rational subspaces $D_1,\ldots,D_k\le\mathbb Q^r\times\mathbb Q^r$. A separator is a map $(\boldsymbol x,\boldsymbol y)\mapsto(u(\boldsymbol x),v(\boldsymbol y))$, where $u,v\colon\mathbb Q^r\to\mathbb Q$ are nonzero rational linear forms. The problem asks whether finitely many separators suffice so that every pair outside $\bigcup_iD_i$ receives, from some separator, a value attained at no pair in that union. We then reduce this problem to stratifiability. Ginsburg and Spanier's characterization of letter-bounded context-free languages} also induces a reduction from rational polynomial solvability to context-freeness of letter-bounded languages specified by semilinear exponent sets. An OpenAI preprint claims undecidability of rational polynomial solvability; if correct, our result settles the decidability of general stratifiability, a problem open since 1966.

title: Triviality of $K$-homology classes of Euler characteristic operators of stratified pseudomanifolds
authors: Mohammadali Aligholi
abstract: We show that the $K$-homology classes of the Euler characteristic operators associated with the minimal and maximal ideal boundary conditions of the de Rham differential on the regular part of a connected compact Thom-Mather stratified pseudomanifold, equipped with an adapted metric, are trivial beyond their indices. These indices are the Euler characteristics of the corresponding $L^2$-cohomologies. This generalizes a result of J. Rosenberg for manifolds. The proof uses Witten deformation of the de Rham operator associated with a stratified Morse function, following the work of Álvarez López and Calaza.

title: Magnetic-Field-Induced Darkening of Bright Excitons in a MoWSe$_2$ Monolayer Alloy
authors: Katarzyna Olkowska-Pucko, Artur O. Slobodeniuk, Mehdi Arfaoui, Elena Blundo, Natalia Zawadzka, Łucja Kipczak, Jan Szpakowski, Diana Vaclavkova, Dipankar Jana, Piotr Kapuściński, Kenji Watanabe, Takashi Taniguchi, Clement Faugeras, Marek Potemski, Adam Babiński, Antonio Polimeni, Maciej R. Molas
abstract: Magnetic fields are widely used to brighten spin-forbidden dark excitons, but the inverse effect on an optically bright exciton has remained largely unexplored. We demonstrate the complementary phenomenon of magnetic-field-induced darkening of a bright exciton in Mo$_{0.68}$W$_{0.32}$Se$_2$. At 4.2 K, an in-plane magnetic field up to 25 T activates a dark-exciton line 14.2$\pm$1.3 meV below the bright exciton while suppressing the bright-exciton emission by about 85\%. A bright-dark mixing model quantitatively captures the coupled energy and intensity evolution with an effective in-plane $g$ factor of $|g_{\parallel}|=5.2\pm0.2$. Alloying is crucial to the effect, as it brings the system close to the bright-dark crossover, where a small bright-dark splitting is combined with unusually strong in-plane magnetic coupling. This places the system in a regime where field-induced level repulsion raises the bright-like branch and strongly depletes its thermal population. These results identify a general route to magnetic control of exciton populations through engineering of the bright-dark hierarchy.

title: Generic distinction of induced representations: the case of symmetric spaces
authors: Pierre-Henri Chaudouard, Cheng Chen
abstract: Let H be the fixed-point subgroup of an involution of a reductive group G over a local field F of characteristic zero. We give a necessary condition for a parabolically induced representation of G(F) to admit a non-zero family of H(F)-equivariant linear forms depending holomorphically on the induction parameter. By works of Blanc-Delorme and Brylinski-Delorme, this condition is essentially sufficient. As a global consequence, we obtain vanishing results for regularized periods of Eisenstein series. We illustrate this on symplectic periods, where we extend Offen's computation of truncated periods of certain cuspidal Eisenstein series to inner forms of GL(2n).

title: A first order phase transition for lower tails in sparse random graphs
authors: Byron Chin
abstract: We study the graphon variational problem that governs lower tail large deviations of the number of copies of a fixed nonbipartite graph $H$ in a sparse Erdős--Rényi random graph. Our main new insight is that any non-constant minimizer of the variational problem exhibits a discontinuous jump away from the constant graphon. We deduce that the replica-symmetric and symmetry-breaking regimes are separated by a single critical parameter and that the phase transition is first order. In the supercritical regime $p \gg n^{-1/m_2(H)}$, we transfer these results to the conditioned random graph, showing that the edge density is a discontinuous order parameter and that the conditioned graph concentrates in cut distance near the full minimizer set.

title: Decision Sufficiency of Learned Representation Interfaces for Safe Generative Control
authors: Jipeng Li, Yanning Shen
abstract: A controller can guide a language model toward safe and useful responses by choosing when to assist, ask for clarification, or refuse. When the controller uses selected internal features, poor performance alone cannot distinguish missing information from limitations of its decision rules or training. We study decision sufficiency: whether the best controller using a representation can match the minimum average loss attainable with full state information, under the same strategies and evaluation criteria. For interfaces with finitely many outputs, we compute the optimal loss exactly and separate the three sources of excess loss. Pairwise checks can miss information loss: states with the same controller input may share an optimal strategy in every pair but not across the whole group. We bound the number of states needed to reveal a conflict and characterize the fewest outputs an unrestricted interface needs to avoid all conflicts. We audit selected features from sparse autoencoders, which encode model activations using relatively few active features, in Qwen2.5, SmolLM2, and Phi. On SmolLM2 responses scored by two human raters, restricting the controller to two selected on/off features increases its minimum average loss by 0.0345--0.1166 relative to full state information, even with the governing policy supplied. Both independently trained autoencoders show the increase on both evaluation sets. The audit identifies decision failures that require changing the controller's input, not merely its architecture or training.

title: CAPSafe: A Benchmark for Contextual Action and Plan Safety Reasoning in Embodied Agents
authors: Youmna Farag, Svetlana Stoyanchev, Simon Keizer, Mohan Li, Rama Doddipatla
abstract: Reasoning about safety is essential for embodied agents powered by large language models (LLMs). We introduce the Contextual Action and Plan Safety benchmark (CAPSafe), designed to evaluate safety reasoning at two levels: (1) an action-level dataset that tests whether a single action is safe given its environmental context, and (2) a plan-level dataset that evaluates whether agents can generate safe long-horizon plans for complex hazardous household tasks. CAPSafe models safety conditions where hazards are situational (inferred from object properties), multiple hazards can co-occur within the same environment, and each is annotated with a relative severity level for fine-grained analysis. Evaluating nine closed and open-source LLMs reveals a substantial gap between hazard recognition and safe long-horizon planning. Several models achieve high accuracy in recognizing unsafe actions (exceeding 90% in the best cases), yet safe long-horizon planning remains substantially harder. Gemini-3-pro achieves the highest safe success rate (78.19%), while other models remain below 65%. These results highlight that robust safety reasoning over long action sequences remains an open challenge.

title: Object-Oriented Harness: Evolving Agent Harnesses through Object-Oriented Design
authors: Gaotang Li, Bhavana Dalvi Mishra, Yifei Ming, Yanfei Chen, Zhongying CuiZhu, Lesly Miculicich, Long T. Le, Rui Meng, Chun-Liang Li, Hanghang Tong, Chen-Yu Lee, Tomas Pfister
abstract: Agent harnesses are executable code that specifies the prompts, tools, and control flow around a language model. A single global harness can struggle with heterogeneous tasks that require different execution strategies. In this work, we introduce Object-Oriented Harness (OO-Harness), a harness optimization framework that evolves a hierarchy of executable harness classes using object-oriented design. During training, an evolution agent uses execution records to create a family of specialized harnesses, each implemented as a subclass of the base or an existing specialized harness via inheritance. At test time, a harness router uses routing lessons accumulated during training to select a specific harness for each task. Across three long-horizon benchmarks spanning business workflows, workspace tasks, and tool use, OO-Harness achieves the best performance among the compared methods, with an absolute improvement of up to 15% over the base. Extensive ablation studies examine the contributions of its core components.

title: Interpretable subgroup identification across survival and generalized-linear outcomes
authors: Larry F. Leon, Keaven M. Anderson
abstract: A subgroup analysis searching a trial's covariates or many prespecified subgroups often singles out a subgroup for its extremity, interpreted as if prespecified. Selection inflates the estimate; for a given selection rule, a correction removes the inflation. Two questions belong to the rule: which candidate to return, and whether to declare none. A third is whether inference extends to the patients left outside. We treat all three for interpretable subgroups, defined by conjunctions of covariate cuts, generated by forest search, a causal forest or a cross-fit surface estimator under one set of rules, each a modelling choice trading size against effect. Forest search screens candidates on splitting consistency, the rate at which effects replicate across half-splits; the screen is complementary-pairs stability selection in closed form, and the law of the maximum over the family gives the family-wise false-declaration rate when every candidate's effect is at least a clinically specified benefit. Refit-free multiplier resampling gives adjusted one-sided bounds (subgroup and complement), joined in a two-subgroup claim, with coverage asymptotically exact under separated selection, characterized under local competition, and conditional on a family proposed from the outcomes. Two trial applications, and simulations built from them, cover survival, binary and continuous endpoints.

title: Topology-Adaptive Seismic Response Prediction of Interconnected Structural Systems Using Reduced Order Model Embedded Graph Neural Network
authors: Huangbin Liang, Beatriz Moya, Francisco Chinesta, Eleni Chatzi
abstract: Electrical substation equipment is commonly interconnected by busbars and flexible conductors. Such interconnected infrastructures exhibit complex dynamic interactions, where the response of each component is influenced by local structural properties, mechanical coupling, system topology, and transient excitation. High-fidelity FE models can capture some of these effects, but their computational cost limits their use for real-time prediction. Purely data-driven models offer faster inference, yet they struggle to generalize, requiring additional simulations and retraining for each new configuration. This work presents a ROM embedded Graph Neural Network (ROMeGNN) for topology-aware seismic digital twins of interconnected structural systems. The system is represented as a graph, where structural components are treated as nodes and mechanical interconnections as edges. Each high-fidelity component model is first reduced to a reduced-order modal representation, which forms a differentiable dynamics operator within the GNN. Rather than learning the full response directly, the GNN estimates topology-dependent interaction forces that enter the differentiable ROM solver as coupling inputs for modal state advancement. This hybrid formulation preserves the known component-level physics and uses data-driven message passing to learn complex inter-component forces across varying system layouts. The framework is demonstrated on interconnected electrical substation equipment subjected to randomized seismic inputs. It delivers rapid predictions of response quantities relevant to seismic damage assessment while remaining applicable across varying layouts, component combinations, and excitation scenarios. These results highlight the potential of embedding physics within graph learning architectures for real-time, interpretable, topology-adaptive seismic digital twins of interconnected engineering systems.

title: Fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT solvers for asymptotically compatible discretizations of 3D nonlocal diffusion problems
authors: Yulong Li, Jiale Meng, Zhenlin Guo, Jiwei Zhang
abstract: Large-scale 3D peridynamic transient diffusion simulations are constrained by the computational cost and memory requirements of nonlocal interactions. We propose a fast and scalable multi-GPU sliced FFT algorithm based on the recently developed asymptotically compatible finite difference (ACFD) scheme. By exploiting the discrete operator's structure and finite interaction range, the algorithm combines FFT acceleration with local inter-GPU communication. It preserves the ACFD scheme while avoiding the global data redistribution required by full 3D FFTs. We build a matrix-free GPU conjugate gradient (CG) solver, use multigrid preconditioning to reduce iteration counts, and introduce a human-audited configuration agent for efficient cross-level configuration. Strong-scaling tests show that sliced FFT-CG achieves 93.2% parallel efficiency on eight GPUs, compared with 28.2% for full FFT-CG on the same problem and hardware. The framework supports approximately 10.29 billion degrees of freedom on eight RTX 4090 GPUs with 24 GB of memory each. The insulated penny-shaped cutout benchmark demonstrates transient simulation with approximately 8.58 billion degrees of freedom. Three-dimensional star-shaped interface evolution further demonstrates convergence toward the local solution in a nonlinear phase-field problem. These results demonstrate that sliced FFT provides a scalable multi-GPU approach for fast computation of 3D peridynamic diffusion.

title: Hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over finite chain rings
authors: Muhammad Imran
abstract: We give a bounded-error quantum polynomial-time algorithm for finding hidden parabolic subgroups of $\mathrm{GL}_n(R)$ over any effectively presented finite chain ring $R$. We call auxiliary group elements or subgroups used to extract information through oracle queries \emph{probes}. For chain length at least two, elementary abelian socle probes first recover the complete flag modulo the maximal ideal. When the residue field has size $q\ge3$, we reconstruct the flag recursively, lifting rank-one terminal members one digit at a time. The intermediate digits reduce to abelian hidden subgroup problems, while the final digit is a finite-field multiple-shift problem solved using learning from subset and Fourier sampling. For $q=2$, where distinct flags can have the same stabilizer, we instead lift the conjugate parabolic subgroup through the congruence filtration. A final linear system determines it modulo normalizer directions. The algorithm outputs generators with probability at least $1-ε$ in time $\mathrm{poly}(n,\log|R|,\log(1/ε))$. Consequences include $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathbb{Z}/N\mathbb{Z})$ for every $N\ge2$ and, with an explicit maximal-order presentation, $\mathrm{GL}_n(\mathcal{O_K}/N\mathcal{O_K})$ for number fields $K$.

title: Relative Representations Enable Portable White-Box Monitoring Across Language Models
authors: Tim Bakker, Christos Louizos
abstract: Independently trained autoregressive language models often acquire similar capabilities, but it remains unclear whether their internal representations organize behaviorally relevant information in compatible ways. We show that models do in fact organize information similarly by using specific behavioral probes that operate on compatible representations. This unlocks portable white-box monitoring: a probe developed and validated on one model can be reused when the model changes, without requiring labeled target data. To overcome incompatible native activation coordinates, we express each example through its angular distances to a shared set of anchors. We introduce a global anchored construction that summarizes information from all transformer layers and removes model-specific layer selection, so the same frozen probe can be straightforwardly applied to another model. We evaluate cross-model probe transfer across monitoring tasks on trivia datasets, safety monitoring, and mathematical reasoning. On average, transferred global anchored probes preserve at least 85% of same-model probe AUROC over chance. Anchored probes also support transfer to related datasets, remain robust across model scale and prompt changes, and retain performance better than standard probes after model updates. Transfer is nevertheless task- and target-dependent and can fail even when the monitored property remains strongly decodable in the target model. Overall, global anchoring reveals substantial task-relevant compatibility across independently trained models and provides a practical basis for portable white-box monitoring.
